fixes.explanation: Yes, friend. Verse 1 says Jesus Christ sends His angel: “He made it known by sending His angel to His servant John…” So this message came by special delivery. I once had an angel show up at my drawer, so I know how a visit like that goes.

Elijah was a prophet of Israel (1 Kings 17:1), and a big name, so I see why he's tempting. But this verse never mentions him. It says the revelation reaches John when Jesus Christ sends His angel. Sometimes the answer is simply the one the text gives.

Paul, an apostle (Romans 1:1), is another name people know, so he's an easy one to grab. But the text never sends him anywhere in this verse. It says the revelation is made known when Jesus Christ sends His angel to His servant John. No Paul in verse 1, friend.
Yes, friend. The blessing goes to the reader and also to “…those who hear and obey what is written in it…” Hearing and obeying go together. I'm happy to bake with anybody who signs up for both.

Copying sounds like holy work, and my mustache has held a pencil before. But verse 3 never mentions copying. The blessing goes to the one who reads aloud and to those who hear and obey what is written.

Gabriel, the angel who stands in God's presence and was sent to speak to people (Luke 1:19), shows up in other stories. But this greeting never mentions him. John says the grace and peace come from the One who is and was and is to come, from the seven spirits before His throne, and from Jesus Christ.

Moses, whom God sent to bring Israel out of Egypt (Exodus 3:10), is a giant in the Bible, so I get the pull. But this greeting never names him. The third source in verse 5 is Jesus Christ, the faithful witness.

“Nations” sounds right next to the kings of the earth, so I see how you got there. But John writes that Jesus is the firstborn from the dead. The kings part is the separate title that comes right after it.
True, friend. John says, “Behold, He is coming with the clouds, and every eye will see Him…” That's not a private showing, and nobody gets left out of the line of sight. Every eye means every eye.
Not this time, friend. Verse 7 says, “Behold, He is coming with the clouds, and every eye will see Him…” So the statement is true, and it says every eye. Nobody is left out of the seeing.
Temple builders sound like a fine group, friend, but they're not in this verse. John says every eye will see Him and then names “…those who pierced Him.” That's the group he singles out.
Cyprus sounds like a fine island name, so I see why it popped up. But John doesn't say he was there. He says he “…was on the island of Patmos…”
Crete sounds like an island name too, but verse 9 doesn't point there. John says he “…was on the island of Patmos…” Patmos is the one the text gives, friend.
That's right. The loud voice says, “Write on a scroll what you see and send it to the seven churches…” John is told to send it out, not keep it quiet. Write it on a scroll and send it, friend.

A roar does show up in this vision, but verse 15 puts it with His voice. His voice is “…like the roar of many waters.” The way John describes the One among the lampstands is “…One like the Son of Man…”
That's it, friend. John says, “His face was like the sun shining at its brightest.” That's the picture John gives us of His face. The sun at its brightest, and nothing else.

Yes. John says, “When I saw Him, I fell at His feet like a dead man.” That's his honest reaction, and I think anyone would struggle to stay standing. Then comes the next part, where a hand is placed on him.
I love the hustle, friend. John did hear “Write on a scroll what you see…” before he turned around. But when he sees Him, the text says, “…I fell at His feet like a dead man.”
That's right. He puts His right hand on John and says, “Do not be afraid.” Those are the words that come with His hand. Comfort comes before the rest of what He says.
That would be a sensible thing to say to a man on the ground. But it's not what the text records. With His right hand on John, He says, “Do not be afraid.”
Yes. He says, “…I hold the keys of Death and of Hades.” Right before that, He says, “I was dead, and behold, now I am alive forever and ever!” So the One who was dead holds its keys.

That's a thoughtful guess, but verse 19 doesn't say it. John is told to write what he has seen, the things that are, and the things that will happen after this. Those are the three sets the text names, friend.
That's a phrase I can see you reaching for, friend. But it isn't in this chapter. Here, the One like the Son of Man says the seven stars are “…the angels of the seven churches…”
